Alex (Support): Hey team — customer reported a big invoice surprise. Their SDK local token tally shows ~1.2k tokens for a session, invoice shows ~1.6k. They only do a short prompt + streaming completion. Can we triage? :eyes:
Tim (SDK): can you paste the exact payload + SDK version? streaming vs non-streaming changes counts sometimes.
Alex (Support): SDK v0.8.4, using node client. Minimal repro attached below. Customer says no tool calls, but there *is* a system message in their app code.
Alex (Support): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \\n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n -d '{"model":"open-rl-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize these notes: ..."}],"stream":true}'
```
Alex (Support): local tokenizer counted prompt=420, completion=800, total=1220. Invoice shows total tokens billed=1620.
Maya (Eng ML): quick checklist: 1) server-inserted system prefixes (for routing/guardrails) 2) function/tool metadata injected post-return 3) streaming stop boundary double-counting bug 4) opaque kv/cache metadata added to metering snapshot.
Tim (SDK): v0.8.4 had a tokenizer mismatch vs backend when streaming stop sends a partial chunk; that was fixed in v0.9.x. Also SDK tokenizer excludes some server-inserted tool metadata by default. Can you confirm whether the customer uses any middleware that rewrites messages?
Alex (Support): customer says no middleware. They do call a short helper that adds the single system message (we included that). No function calls.
Lina (Billing): can you share the invoice id and a meter snapshot? I can pull the raw metering rows and match timestamps.
Alex (Support): invoice #INV-2026-9987, customer provided their local trace id trace-9f7a.
metrology-bot: Metering snapshot generated: https://internal.redwood/metrology/snapshots/trace-9f7a (auto-posted)
Maya (Eng ML): I looked at the snapshot quickly — there's a ~380-token prefix attributed to "server:prefill_kv" in the meter rows. That explains the delta. It's not in the user's messages because it's injected by the runtime for same-session KV prefill.
Tim (SDK): ah — runtime prefill can include: model session primers, safety prompts, and tool-call provenance blobs. SDK local tokenizer won't see runtime-only inserts. That matches the +400 tokens.
Alex (Support): customer surprised because they never saw those tokens in their app. How should we explain and what are mitigation options?
Maya (Eng ML): Explanation: the runtime can augment requests with short server-only metadata (prefill KV, routing prefixes, safety primers). Those are counted in metering. Mitigations: a) opt into a reduced prefill profile (config flag) b) pin to a dedicated runtime pool (no runtime prefill) c) upgrade SDK to v0.9.x which surfaces a "meter-preview" header for local estimates.
Tim (SDK): practical steps: 1) ask customer to reproduce with a raw curl (no SDK) to verify counts. 2) try SDK v0.9.2 that accepts header X-Redwood-Meter-Preview: true and returns meter-preview in response. 3) if they want immediate relief, submit a billing review and enable the quieter prefill profile for their org (Lina).
Lina (Billing): I can open a billing review once we have the raw metrology snapshot + curl repro. If the prefill came from runtime change in the last week we can apply a one-time credit and advise the customer on config.
Alex (Support): sending repro steps to customer now: 1) run the curl above (replace token) 2) collect response headers and raw body 3) provide the metrology snapshot link and invoice id.
Tim (SDK): note: if they're streaming, ask them to send the stream session id. There's a known edge where stream re-announce events produced extra meter rows that backend aggregates differently. Fixed in 0.9.2.
Maya (Eng ML): internal action: I'll add a short note to the metering runbook explaining server-prefill rows and where to look. Also will file a follow-up to make prefill behavior more visible in Console.
Lina (Billing): assigned billing review to me. I'll wait for the raw snapshot + curl.
Alex (Support): thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and attach the snapshot. :thumbsup:
Tim (SDK): if customer wants to test SDK change quickly, they can do: ```js
// upgrade to v0.9.2
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
const res = await client.generate({messages, stream: false, headers: {"X-Redwood-Meter-Preview":"true"}});
console.log(res.meter_preview);
```
Alex (Support): I'll follow up after customer returns repro.
